ruling.recommended_action: Route F3 (22:54–23:03 off-route segment) to a human reviewer: determine whether the actual driven path corresponds to Guillemard Road, the road the rider agreed to at 22:51; if the segment ran elsewhere, apply RD-2 (2.13 km × $1.4102/km = $3.00 refund via voucher) and add the RD-6 account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
The rider's complaint is that the driver took a longer way round and charged more than the app showed, so the case turns on whether the 2.13 km extra on the 22:54–23:03 segment is excused [F1][F3][RD-1]. Under RD-4 no incident was recorded and a speed band alone cannot exempt a segment, so the traffic record does not excuse this segment [F12][F15][RD-4]. The only candidate excuse is the rider's own agreement: the driver asked at 22:51 "mind if I go round via Guillemard Road?" and the rider replied "Sure, go ahead" — a rider message sent before the 22:54:50 segment start on a complete, fully timestamped chat record [F8][F9][F10][RD-5].

That agreement is a specific named-road authorisation ("go round via Guillemard Road"), not a general "whichever way is faster" mandate, so per RD-5(2) it covers driving on Guillemard Road only, and the record must tie the off-route segment to that road [F8][F9][RD-5]. The fact table carries no road name for the driven path; the driver's after-the-trip statement names Guillemard Road, but a driver's assertion is not rider consent evidence for scope and the statement itself adds nothing the chat did not already contain [F11][RD-5]. Timing alone therefore cannot establish that the 2.13 km of extra driving at 22:54–23:03 was on Guillemard Road, and nothing places the segment elsewhere either; the scope correspondence is undetermined (G13) [F3][F8][F9][RD-5].

This undetermined finding controls the outcome: if the segment was on the agreed road it is exempt and no refund is due, whereas if it was not it counts and 2.13 km of extra metered distance is refundable under RD-2 at this trip's distance fare rate, 2.13 km × $1.4102/km = $3.00 [F3][F4][RD-2]. Because the case also involves a driver with 2 upheld route disputes in 90 days, the segment finding also decides whether the RD-6 account flag attaches, so the record cannot be resolved by the judge and must go to a person [F18][RD-6]. No stop was requested by the rider in this segment, so RD-3 does not apply [F8][F9][RD-3].
